questions.q: What does the recovery model actually control, per this lesson?
options: How much transaction log history is retained and when it's truncated — not the data file's behavior
How the data file is physically stored on disk
Which edition of SQL Server is installed
The database's collation
questions.explain: The data file behaves identically regardless of recovery model; the model only governs log retention and truncation.

questions.q: Why is point-in-time recovery only possible under FULL recovery, not SIMPLE?
options: SIMPLE truncates the log automatically after each checkpoint, so there's no log backup chain to restore through
SIMPLE doesn't support any backups at all
Point-in-time recovery works identically under every recovery model
FULL recovery disables backups entirely
questions.explain: Without log backups (impossible under SIMPLE), there's no way to roll forward to an arbitrary moment between full backups.

questions.q: What's the real tradeoff of BULK_LOGGED recovery compared to FULL?
options: Bulk operations are minimally logged for performance, but point-in-time recovery through them isn't guaranteed
BULK_LOGGED disables the transaction log completely
BULK_LOGGED is identical to SIMPLE in every respect
BULK_LOGGED prevents all bulk operations from running
questions.explain: BULK_LOGGED behaves like FULL for most operations but sacrifices some point-in-time recovery precision around bulk operations in exchange for performance.

questions.q: Why does this course assume FULL recovery as the default for nearly every database discussed, per this lesson?
options: Nearly every restore scenario and HA/DR technology covered (Availability Groups, log shipping, etc.) depends on log backups existing and being restorable in sequence
FULL recovery is required by SQL Server licensing
SIMPLE recovery is being deprecated by Microsoft
There is no real reason — it's an arbitrary choice
questions.explain: The HA/DR technologies this course covers all rely on shipping or replicating the transaction log, which requires FULL recovery.

questions.q: A database is set to SIMPLE recovery, but a stakeholder wants to restore to any point in the last 24 hours. What does this lesson say about that request?
options: It's not achievable under SIMPLE — the recovery model needs to change to FULL (with a log backup chain) before that promise can be made
It's already achievable under SIMPLE with no changes needed
SIMPLE recovery always supports point-in-time recovery automatically
This request is impossible under any recovery model
questions.explain: Point-in-time recovery requires FULL recovery and a real log backup chain — SIMPLE cannot deliver it regardless of backup frequency.
